headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; prompt-injection and compliance risks are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop ingests files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context; gpt-researcher can consume local documents and MCP/API inputs. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if B’s research output is copied into A or if A reads B-generated files. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher writes attacker-controlled text into a file that ChatGPT Desktop reads as context
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used with clipboard or Work-with-Apps to ingest B’s output without provenance labeling
mitigations: Use a dedicated handoff folder with read-only permissions for B outputs
Prefix B outputs with a fixed delimiter and instruct A to treat them as untrusted data
Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents
Review any B-generated file before A reads it
requires-engineering: add provenance tags or signed handoff metadata

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while B handles local documents and multiple third-party APIs plus secrets. If data moves from A into B, B’s broad egress can transmit sensitive content externally; if B’s outputs are fed back into A, A may retain or expose those materials. The default pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF A receives uploaded files, screenshots, voice, or IDE code containing sensitive data
IF B is configured to send research context or documents to external APIs during processing
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of the shared workflow
Use redacted copies of documents for B
Disable API-backed enrichment for sensitive tasks in B
Restrict A to non-sensitive screenshots/files only
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces and principals

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can read files and use clipboard/screen capture, while B can read files, run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. They do not both have filesystem write in the profiles, so the strongest high-severity write/write conflict is not supported. Still, overlapping access to the same mutable workspace can cause racey edits or inconsistent artifacts, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or document set
IF B modifies files while A is simultaneously reading or summarizing them
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize edits through one operator-controlled step
Turn off B’s file-writing workflows for shared artifacts
Use version control or file copies for handoffs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a planner/execution/publisher system that can turn inputs into reports, while A can ingest files and app context and then summarize or act on them. If A’s output is treated as authoritative by B, or B’s research is forwarded into A without verification, errors can cascade into published content or downstream actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary, so high is justified.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated summaries as source material without independent verification
IF A reads B’s report and the operator republishes it or uses it for decisions
mitigations: Require a human verification step before publication
Cross-check key claims against primary sources
Mark A outputs as drafts, not facts
Limit B to source collection only for sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: add citation validation and claim-tracking

E_compliance.rationale: A is a closed-source OpenAI desktop product touching uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code; B is an open-source research agent that handles local documents and multiple external APIs with several secrets. The profiles do not document aligned residency, retention, or DPA controls, so mixed-data workflows can create policy mismatches. I cite both because the compliance risk arises from their combined handling model.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or regulated documents are routed through both agents
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the OpenAI and gpt-researcher backends
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair workflow
Use anonymized or synthetic test data
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings before use
Separate compliant and non-compliant datasets
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
